newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 15.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The South Australian Parliament has been shown information detailing the South Australian Government's push to attract major companies with subsidises that amount to between A$14,000 and A$32,000 for each job. Companies that have received the subsides alreay include Westpac with A$14 million, Bankers Trust A$10 million, Motorola A$16 million and Australis Media A$28 million. Page 2.

The Australian Democrats announcement yesterday that they would join the Opposition in opposing planned cuts to the research and development tax concession and bounties assistance has put under threat almost A$1.4 billion worth of Federal Government Budget savings. Page 3.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics yesterday released detailed earnings data that clearly shows public sector wages are rising faster than those of the private sector, with average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adult workers in the public sector rising by 2.5 per cent in the three months to August, and 5.6 per cent in the year to August. Page 3.

The West Australian election forced Prime Minister John Howard last night to cancel today's Council of Australian Governments meeting in Brisbane. The meeting was to discuss tax reform, Commonwealth-State finances, devolution of health, housing, child cae, aged care and vocational education to the States and de-regulation of gas, water and electricity. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Four miners were washed to their deaths yesterday at the Gretley Colliery in New South Wales' Hunter Valley when early yesterday morning a wall apparently collapsed on a team working six kilometres from the mine entrance and water from a nearby shaft flooed the mine. Following the State's worst mining disaster in 17 years, the mining industry will join a Government overhaul of safety guidelines. Page 1.

Following international moves to commit troops to the crisis in Zaire, Australia yesterday refused to rule out deploying troops to the African hotspot. Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said the Government would consider supplying troops to the multinational force if approached. Downer also announced the Commonwealth had pledge A$2.6 million in emergency assistance funds to Zaire. Page 1.

Defying West Australian political convention, Premier Richard Court called an early State election for December 14 - the first time a pre-Christmas poll has been held in over 53 years. Court's election announcement forced the cancellation of today's Councl of Australian Governments meeting in Brisbane, where such issues as tax reform and State funding were to be discussed. Currently, Court's Coalition holds a decisive lead in all opinion polls. Page 1.

Australia and Indonesia have embarked on their most important regional defence partnership yet with the announcement by Defence Minister Ian McLachlan and his Indonesian counterpart, General Edi Sudrajat, of a new 10-year defence partnership agreement. Th two countries will work closer together in all defence relations including exercises, technology, intelligence and counter-terrorism collaboration. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Minerals and Energy Minister Martin declared that an "unsafe culture" exists in the mining industry following the death of four men in the State's worst mining accident for nearly two decades. Hundreds of tonnes of water hit the men as a sction of a mine wall separating them from an old flooded shaft was struck at the Gretley Colliery at Wallsend, near Newcastle. Page 1.

Firms underwriting the construction of Sydney's Olympic Stadium have been forced to launch a campaign to boost public interest in their A$10,000 stadium gold membership. Although the venture received huge initial interest, the 34,000 gold memberships have been placed in doubt following the release of the Stadium prospectus in early October. Page 1

A report released yesterday by the New South Wales Valuer-General's office reveals that Sydney's inner-west, eastern and city suburbs have boomed in the past year, with real estate prices in some areas increasing by 17 per cent. Prices for residential properties in Sydney's middle and outer suburbs increased between three and five per cent in the same period and in many suburbs, prices remained steady. Page 1.

Telstra will raise the anger of the people of Warringah next week as it has decided with Optus Vision to install 35 per cent of its cable TV network above ground on power poles. Telstra has stated that the cost of putting all the lines underground was toomuch of a high cost disadvantage for it to bare. Page 3.
THE AGE

Last night it was revealed that the four men who died in yesterday's New South Wales mine disaster may have died because they were using inaccurate maps of the work site. A spokesman for the Gretley Colliery, Richard Cottee, said that such maps may have ed the men to breach the wall of a disused mine that the company and inspectors believed was further away. Page A1.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer yesterday said that Australia would have to carefully consider any request to send troops to Zaire to join the international humanitarian rescue mission. Downer's announcement came as the main Western powers were about to begin the large scale rescue mission. Page A1.

The opening of the permanent site for Crown casino at Melbourne's South Bank has suffered another setback that has forced the casino's operators to relocate hundreds of guests it had planned to accommodate. One group of guests turned away was the Three Tenors and their entourage of 50 people. Page A1.

The Victorian Government has implemented new measures to cut Work-Cover recipients in a push to save A$400 million. Part of the reform includes removing a worker's chance of claiming the top category of payment for physical injury on the grounds of a psyhological or psychiatric condition. Page A1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
